input: Start a daily gratitude log in a small notebook

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The time of day chosen (morning vs. evening) shapes the prompts, tone, and how the habit gets anchored to an existing routine.
The number of gratitude items per entry and whether entries are single words, sentences, or longer reflections determines how much structure and space is needed.
Whether the user wants free-form writing or guided prompts changes how the notebook pages should be set up.
Whether the user already has a notebook or needs to choose/buy one affects the very first action to take.
Knowing if this is strictly private or occasionally shared (e.g., with a partner or therapist) affects how personal and candid the entries will be.
A target streak length or time commitment (e.g., 5 minutes max, 30-day challenge) determines how ambitious the habit design should be.
Understanding what the user hopes to gain — reduced stress, greater positivity, self-awareness — helps tailor prompts and milestones to reinforce the right outcomes.

gold.taskTitle: Start a daily gratitude log in a notebook
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to establish a daily habit of writing gratitude entries in a small physical notebook.

questions.title: What time of day will you write in it?
questions.description: Identify whether the user plans to write in the morning, evening, or another specific time, so the habit can be anchored to an existing routine.

questions.title: How many items will you write per entry?
questions.description: Determine the target number of gratitude items per session (e.g., 3 bullet points, 5 sentences) to define the scope of each entry.

questions.title: Do you prefer free writing or structured prompts?
questions.description: Establish whether the user wants blank space to write freely or pre-written prompts on each page to guide their reflections.

questions.title: Do you already have a notebook ready to use?
questions.description: Find out if the user has a notebook on hand or still needs to select and obtain one, which determines the immediate first action.

questions.title: Will this log be completely private, just for you?
questions.description: Clarify whether the journal is strictly personal or might be shared with someone, which affects how open and candid the entries will be.

questions.title: Is there a streak or duration goal you have in mind?
questions.description: Understand if the user is aiming for a specific challenge length (e.g., 30 days, 3 months) or an open-ended ongoing habit, to shape the commitment level.

questions.title: What do you most hope to feel or gain from this?
questions.description: Identify the user's core motivation — such as less stress, more positivity, or greater self-awareness — to tailor prompts and milestones accordingly.
